newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies close sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies close sharply lower.

text.p: Actively traded months of CME hog and pork belly futures tumbled sharply late as commercial selling touched off fund sell stops late, traders said.

Hog futures closed 1.300 cent per lb lower to 0.100 higher with February off most at 76.300 cents. Pork bellies ended 1.750 cent lower to 0.525 higher with thinly traded deferreds holding earlier gains and February off 1.475 at 74.874 cents.

Commercial selling prompted by expectations of falling cash hog prices next week pushed through a large fund buy order and prices fell. Other months quickly sold with sell stops adding to the setback, traders said.
Expecations are that hogs held back by recent bitter cold weather will start to be marketed early next week.
"When those temperatures moderate, you are going to hurt that (cash) price," said Karen Curry, livestock analyst with Rosenthal Collins.
Curry also noted that demand for pork products has not been that good. As a result, packers are losing money and they want to bid lower for hogs.
February hit sell stops under 76.800 cents and April followed with stops under 75.650 cents, traders said.

Rand Financials were on both sides of the market with Cargill Investor Services and R.J. O'Brien sellers. The commercial division of Rand sold into the large fund buy order from the fund division of Rand. LFG and Rand sold April, pit sources said.

In hog options, LIT division of First Options bought February 76 puts early. R.J. O'Brien bought February 80 calls and sold 72 puts later. Volatility was down in February and April, pit sources added.
Pork bellies showed short covering support at times but also fell late when hog futures broke, sources noted.

Technical sell stops were again touched on the late setback. Expectations of increased hog marketings and slaughter rates next week kept a lid on gains, especially since demand for product has remained sluggigh, traders said.

Even with the recent weather-reduced hog slaughter, cash belly prices have shown only a steady to firm trend. Product has also moved into storage despite the kill pace and more product will likely have to be put into storage if production rises sharply next week, they added.
R.J. O'Brien sold early while Prudential Securities and Cargill Investor Services notably sold late, pit sources said.
